subject: BeaconHealth — traffic mosaic & session samples for dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Alexei Morozov <alexei@beaconhealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing request — sample traffic attached

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for taking this call last week. As discussed, BeaconHealth is evaluating a dedicated cluster to serve a clinical-assistant product (patient Q&A + summarization). We attached a small slice of traffic (beacon_sample_traffic_202702.csv) — 7 days, token-level sampling by session. High level notes: 1) average prompt length ~120 tokens, 2) median response length ~420 tokens, 3) ~18% of sessions are streaming (progressive long summaries), 4) we expect a 6am–10am and 6pm–10pm dayparting peak in US ET.

Can you point us to the specific fields you need for a pre-sales sizing (concurrency, session duration, burst windows, prompt buckets)? Also, procurement wants a rough SLO/monitoring ask we can include in the internal purchase request.

Attached: beacon_sample_traffic_202702.csv (sample), prompt_snippets_v1.txt (representative prompts).

Appreciate it,
Alexei Morozov
Head of Product, BeaconHealth
alexei@beaconhealth.ai

--
Attachment: beacon_sample_traffic_202702.csv (text/csv, 78 KB)
Attachment: prompt_snippets_v1.txt (text/plain, 6 KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Alexei Morozov <alexei@beaconhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — sample traffic attached

Alexei —

Thanks for the slice, that helps. Quick clarifications so we size conservatively:

- Concurrency vs sessions: does the CSV include session-level concurrency (concurrent open sessions) or only per-request timestamps? If you have session open/close markers that’s ideal.
- Streaming behavior: for the 18% streaming sessions, are responses streamed token-by-token (server-side streaming) or chunked every ~200 tokens? Also confirm typical streaming p99 response length.
- Retry rates / FN requests: are clients retrying at the edge (we saw ~1.5% retry rate in the sample) or is that transient labeling?
- SLA target: what p50/p95/p99 end-to-end generation latency targets do you want for the primary route? Is p99 <= 1.2s acceptable for short prompts (<256 tokens) and p99 <= 4s for long summarization flows?

I’ve attached our SLO template (slo_matrix_template.xlsx) and a short checklist that helps us map token economics to GPU-hours. Can we do a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through key rows? If yes, propose 11:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Direct: (415) 555-0184
Principal Solutions, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: slo_matrix_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet, 12 KB)

From: Alexei Morozov <alexei@beaconhealth.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@beaconhealth.ai>, Ops Team <ops@beaconhealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 15:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — sample traffic attached

Sean — thanks, quick answers inline: 

- The CSV is per-request timestamps; we added session_id in column B in v2 (sending a small followup sample). Our sessions average ~3.2 requests.
- Streaming: we stream token-by-token via SSE for long summaries. p99 streamed response length is ~1,800 tokens; p50 ~420.
- Retries: we see ~0.8% client retries (mostly network blips).
- SLA: p99 <= 3.5s end-to-end for generation is what the product team is targeting for long flows; for short Q&A we’re targeting p99 <= 800ms.

We’re happy to take the 11:00 PT slot tomorrow — adding ops and procurement on the invite.

Alexei
--

Note: followup sample with session_id coming separately.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BeaconHealth — traffic mosaic & session samples for dedicated sizing

Team — pulling a quick playbook summary before the call with BeaconHealth 11:00 PT Monday. My read from Alexei's numbers:

- Traffic shape: clear bimodal dayparting (US ET peaks), average session 3 requests, 18% of sessions are streaming with long responses (~1.8k tokens p99).
- SLO ask: p99 3.5s for long flows, p99 800ms for short Q&A. That pushes us toward reserved capacity with aggressive KV/prefix caching and a streaming-optimized model variant.

Assumptions for first-pass sizing (ballpark):
- Model target: 7B–13B quantized (vram-efficient) if Beacon prioritizes cost; 70–90 tokens/sec decode on A100-ish kernels for long-streaming flows.
- Concurrency baseline: plan for 450 concurrent short Q&A sessions at peak and ~90 concurrent long-streaming sessions (since streaming ties up decoder for longer).
- Buffer for retries/overhead: +15% headroom.

Actions: Karthik — can you produce a 2-column estimate: reserved GPU count (8xA100 eq) vs expected sustained RPS and monthly GPU-hours? Laura — please draft an ops checklist for canary routing (prefix cache warmup, streaming routing, fallbacks). Sean — I’ll handle procurement-facing SLO wording for the quote.

Marissa
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 14:00:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: BeaconHealth — traffic mosaic & session samples for dedicated sizing

Thanks — quick estimate below (very rough, draft for call notes):

- Baseline assumptions: peak short-QPS = 450 concurrent sessions → ~1,350 concurrent requests (avg 3 req/session). Long-streaming concurrent sessions = 90 (p99 length 1.8k tokens).
- Model choice: Recommend quantized 13B variant (good balance decode throughput + quality for summarization).
- Fleet suggestion (reserved): 6 × high-memory GPU nodes (8x A100 eq each) with autoscale headroom to +2 nodes for spike/burst.
- Estimated sustained GPU-hours (month): 6 nodes × 24 × 30 = 4,320 GPU-node hours; with typical occupancy (60%) and decoding load, we estimate ~2,600 billable GPU-hours/month.
- Cost/headroom notes: include prefix KV cache and continuous batching to reduce token cost by ~25% on sustained traffic. Recommend a 2-week canary with traffic ramping 10%→50%→100% over 72h to validate tail latency.

Attachments: proposed_fleet_profile.pdf (contains per-route stitching and warmup playbook).

I’ll upload a short slide with the math before the 11:00 PT call.

—Karthik
Pre-sales, Redwood Inference
